paragraphs: Training several tasks together can change which solutions a neural network prefers. This paper studies shallow ReLU networks that fit their training data while minimizing the sum of squared weights. Its central question concerns the resulting inductive bias: how this preference for small weights shapes the functions learned for individual tasks.

For inputs with a single variable, the authors prove that multi-task interpolation solutions are almost always unique. They also coincide with minimum-norm interpolation solutions in a Sobolev reproducing kernel Hilbert space. This contrasts with the stated single-task setting, whose corresponding minimum-norm problem lies in a different kind of function space and generally has multiple solutions.

For inputs with several variables, the paper establishes a related, approximate connection when the number of tasks is large. Learning then resembles squared-norm minimization using a fixed kernel determined by the optimal neurons. These results explain how sharing a network across tasks can produce kernel-like behavior, with exact and approximate conclusions applying in different settings.
neurips-2024-a-new-neural-kernel-regime-.tldr: Multi-task learning in minimum-weight shallow ReLU networks produces kernel-like solutions, with almost-always uniqueness proved for single-variable inputs.

paragraphs: Searching for useful discrete sequences is important in areas such as protein engineering and drug design. These problems can require choosing among many possibilities without gradients that indicate how to improve a candidate. Bayesian optimization is attractive because it aims to make effective use of a limited number of evaluations of the unknown objective.

The paper surveys high-dimensional Bayesian optimization and identifies obstacles to comparing existing methods. Published approaches use substantially different experimental setups, while technical barriers make algorithms difficult to reproduce or apply to practical problems. Consequently, evaluating methods together requires a common framework and a consistent collection of objectives.

The authors provide both: a unified environment for testing a broad range of optimizers and standardized black-box functions representing chemistry and biology applications. Two extensible software libraries, poli and poli-baselines, support these components and allow new objectives or optimizers to be added. The contribution is infrastructure for more reproducible comparisons and practical experimentation; the abstract does not identify a universally best optimization method.
neurips-2024-a-survey-and-benchmark-of-h.tldr: This survey and benchmark standardize evaluation of high-dimensional discrete Bayesian optimization through shared objectives and extensible software.

paragraphs: Federated learning becomes harder when participating clients need different model architectures or perform different tasks. Methods that assume everyone uses the same model for the same objective cannot directly accommodate this diversity. FedSAK addresses this problem by organizing federated learning as a collection of related client-specific tasks.

Each client separates its local model into a feature extractor and a prediction head. Clients can select which structures to share according to their particular heterogeneity and upload those structures to the server. The server uses a tensor trace norm to discover low-rank structure among the models. This provides a way to learn relationships across clients while allowing flexibility in what they contribute.

The authors derive convergence and generalization bounds in non-convex settings, giving theoretical support alongside practical evaluation. Across six real-world datasets, FedSAK is reported to outperform thirteen advanced federated learning methods. The stated results support flexible coupling as a useful approach when collaboration must accommodate differences in both model design and task requirements.
neurips-2024-a-swiss-army-knife-for-hete.tldr: FedSAK uses low-rank relationships among selectively shared model structures to support federated learning across heterogeneous architectures and tasks.

paragraphs: Reducing differences in model performance across sensitive groups can come at the expense of overall accuracy. The size of this trade-off depends on the dataset, including its imbalances and biases. This paper therefore asks how practitioners can estimate the fairness and accuracy combinations achievable on their own data.

The proposed approach approximates a dataset-specific trade-off curve using the You-Only-Train-Once framework. This reduces the computational burden of training many separate models to explore different compromises. The authors also develop a method for quantifying uncertainty in the estimated curve, supported by statistical guarantees. That uncertainty matters because estimation errors could otherwise lead to mistaken conclusions about fairness or model quality.

Experiments cover tabular data, images, and language, including Adult, CelebA, and Jigsaw. The authors report reliable estimates of optimum achievable trade-offs and show that the approach can expose suboptimality in leading fairness methods. The resulting curve gives practitioners evidence for auditing a model relative to what appears achievable on its particular dataset.
neurips-2024-achievable-fairness-on-your.tldr: The paper estimates dataset-specific fairness–accuracy trade-offs efficiently and quantifies uncertainty to support more reliable model audits.

paragraphs: Multi-objective reinforcement learning must balance several goals, often by requiring a user to specify preferences at deployment. Choosing those preferences can be difficult: people may recognize desirable behavior in demonstrations without knowing how to express the corresponding trade-off explicitly. This paper proposes an offline adaptation framework that uses several demonstrations to indicate the intended behavior.

The framework does not assume handcrafted target preferences. Instead, the demonstrations implicitly communicate the preferences of the desired policy. This changes the information users must provide, replacing an explicit specification of competing objectives with examples of what they want the policy to do.

The authors also extend the approach to safety-critical objectives by using safe demonstrations, even when safety thresholds are unknown. Empirical evaluations on offline multi-objective and safe tasks show policies that align with the intended preferences while satisfying constraints implied by the demonstrations. The safety result is tied to this demonstrated information and the evaluated tasks; it is presented as an empirical capability of the framework.
neurips-2024-an-offline-adaptation-frame.tldr: This offline reinforcement learning framework uses demonstrations to infer objective preferences and accommodate implied safety constraints without explicit target weights or known thresholds.

paragraphs: Medical vision-language models combine image interpretation with language-based responses, creating opportunities for automated and personalized healthcare. CARES examines whether these models are trustworthy across a broader set of concerns than answering medical questions alone. It evaluates five dimensions: trustfulness, fairness, safety, privacy, and robustness.

The benchmark contains approximately 41,000 question-answer pairs spanning sixteen medical image modalities and twenty-seven anatomical regions. It includes both closed questions and questions requiring open-ended answers. This breadth provides a common evaluation resource for examining model behavior across varied medical content and response formats, rather than relying on a single narrow task.

The evaluated models show recurring trustworthiness problems. The authors report factual inaccuracies, unequal behavior across demographic groups, vulnerability to attacks, and limited privacy awareness. These findings identify several distinct weaknesses that matter when considering future deployment. CARES contributes a publicly released benchmark and code for investigating those weaknesses systematically, making trustworthiness itself an explicit evaluation target for medical vision-language research.
neurips-2024-cares-a-comprehensive-bench.tldr: CARES evaluates medical vision-language models across five trustworthiness dimensions and finds recurring problems with factuality, fairness, attacks, and privacy awareness.

paragraphs: Video anomaly systems need to do more than flag unusual footage if people are to understand what happened and ask useful follow-up questions. HAWK uses an interactive visual-language model to interpret anomalies. It addresses both limited semantic understanding in existing systems and the shortage of training data for varied open-world situations.

The approach explicitly incorporates motion because abnormal and normal videos can differ in how things move. An auxiliary consistency loss links the motion and video representations, encouraging the video branch to attend to motion information. The framework also establishes supervision between motion and its language description, helping connect observed movement to an explanation a user can understand.

The authors annotate more than 8,000 anomaly videos with descriptions and create 8,000 question-answer pairs for open-world questions. These resources support both descriptive and interactive training. Reported results surpass existing baselines in video description generation and question answering, supporting the value of motion-aware learning for explaining anomalies as well as responding to users.
neurips-2024-hawk-learning-to-understand.tldr: HAWK combines motion-aware visual-language modeling with new annotations to improve video anomaly descriptions and question answering.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether hidden categories of tokens can be recovered by observing how tokens interact. Its setting assumes that N tokens belong to a small number of classes and that an interaction function depends only on the classes of its arguments. The goal is to reconstruct those memberships from finitely many observations of the function.

The analysis separates computational difficulty from the amount of information required. In general, the problem is NP-complete. For random instances, however, roughly N log N samples suffice to identify the partition. Thus, sparse observations can contain enough information even though solving the unrestricted problem is computationally difficult.

The authors then study whether learning token embeddings through gradient flow can reveal the same hidden structure. They establish that this is possible in certain settings with roughly N² log² N samples. This is a conditional learning result with a larger sufficient sample scale than the information-theoretic result. Together, the findings distinguish identifiable structure from structure recoverable through the particular learning dynamics analyzed.
neurips-2024-learning-partitions-from-co.tldr: The paper distinguishes when token classes are identifiable from sparse interactions from when gradient-flow learning can recover them.

paragraphs: Representing a scene with 3D Gaussians can enable fast rendering, but large scenes may require millions of points and substantial storage. LightGaussian aims to make these representations smaller while preserving visual quality and improving rendering efficiency. It tackles several sources of redundancy within the representation.

First, the method estimates each Gaussian’s global importance to reconstruction and applies pruning followed by recovery. It then uses knowledge distillation and pseudo-view augmentation to represent spherical harmonic coefficients at a lower degree. Finally, significance-aware vector quantization reduces the bitwidth of the Gaussian representation with minimal reported accuracy loss. These stages compress both the collection of Gaussians and the information stored for them.

On Mip-NeRF 360 and Tank & Temple, the authors report average compression of fifteen times and an increase from 144 to 237 frames per second within the 3D-GS framework. They also show that the pruning approach can be adapted to Scaffold-GS. The findings support compression as a route to both smaller scene storage and faster rendering.
neurips-2024-lightgaussian-unbounded-3d-.tldr: LightGaussian combines pruning, distillation, and quantization to report fifteenfold average scene compression while increasing rendering speed.

paragraphs: A language model’s key-value cache saves computations by retaining states for earlier tokens, but its memory use grows with sequence length. MiniCache compresses this cache across network layers. Its starting observation is that neighboring layers in the middle-to-deep portion of a model often have highly similar cached states.

To merge states, MiniCache separates vector magnitude from direction, interpolates directions, and preserves the original lengths. A retention mechanism leaves highly distinct state pairs unmerged, protecting information that is less redundant. The method requires no training and can complement other compression approaches, including quantization and sparsity.

Evaluations span several language-model families and benchmarks. For LLaMA-2-7B on ShareGPT, cross-layer merging achieves a 1.53-fold compression ratio. Combined with four-bit quantization, the reported ratio reaches up to 5.02-fold, with approximately fivefold throughput and a 41% smaller memory footprint than the full FP16 cache baseline, while maintaining near-lossless performance. These are reported evaluation outcomes, showing how reducing redundancy across depth can complement compression within cached states.
neurips-2024-minicache-kv-cache-compress.tldr: MiniCache reduces language-model cache memory by merging similar states across layers while retaining distinctive states and complementing quantization.

paragraphs: Predicting drug-target interactions can help identify possible therapeutics and understand how compounds act. MOTIVE provides a graph dataset for this task that combines recorded relationships with Cell Painting features. The motivation is that cell-based measurements can capture complex interaction effects that complement the physical interactions modeled by structure-based approaches.

The dataset contains Cell Painting features for 11,000 genes and 3,600 compounds, together with relationships drawn from seven public databases. It supplies random splits as well as cold-source and cold-target splits. The latter settings test predictions involving new drugs or new genes, making generalization to previously unseen entities an explicit part of evaluation.

In the reported benchmarks, graph neural networks using Cell Painting features consistently outperform models based only on graph structure, feature-based models, and topological heuristics. This supports combining cellular features with relational information for the evaluated prediction tasks. MOTIVE’s contribution is both a biological graph resource and an evaluation setup for developing more reliable models of interactions involving unfamiliar compounds or genes.
neurips-2024-motive-a-drug-target-intera.tldr: MOTIVE combines Cell Painting features and drug-target relationships to benchmark predictions, including interactions involving new drugs or genes.

paragraphs: Many scientific and machine-learning computations require applying a function of a matrix to a vector. Examples include Gaussian sampling, Gaussian process regression, and analysis of Hessian spectra. Krylov subspace methods approximate this operation, and the classical Lanczos method for matrix functions often performs surprisingly well compared with newer alternatives.

The paper provides a theoretical explanation for that performance. For a natural class of rational functions, it proves that Lanczos-FA achieves an error within a multiplicative factor of the best error possible for a Krylov subspace method. The comparison therefore concerns the quality of its approximation within this family of methods.

The factor depends on the degree of the rational function’s denominator and the matrix’s condition number, but it does not depend on the iteration count. This gives a qualified near-optimality guarantee whose factor does not grow with additional iterations. The authors emphasize its relevance to functions that admit good rational approximations, such as the matrix square root, connecting the theorem to practically useful matrix computations.
neurips-2024-nearly-optimal-approximatio.tldr: For a class of rational functions, Lanczos-FA matches the best Krylov approximation error up to a factor independent of iteration count.

paragraphs: Human pose and shape datasets describe bodies in different ways, including meshes, skeletons, and dense pose annotations. This makes combining their supervision difficult. The paper proposes a common formulation for estimating a human body from one image that can directly use these heterogeneous sources.

The model learns a continuous field of point-localizer functions. At both training and test time, it can be queried about an arbitrary point within the human volume and return that point’s estimated 3D location. Each localizer is a differently parameterized convolutional detector based on a 3D heatmap. This makes the prediction interface flexible enough to accommodate different annotation schemes without converting between them.

When a parametric body representation is needed, an efficient post-processing step fits an SMPL-family model to predicted joints and vertices. Using this approach, the authors train large-scale mesh and skeleton estimators and report substantial improvements over the state of the art on several public benchmarks. The contribution connects flexible supervision with a continuous body representation that can also produce conventional parametric outputs.
neurips-2024-neural-localizer-fields-for.tldr: Neural Localizer Fields unify heterogeneous human-body annotations through a continuous model that predicts the 3D location of arbitrary body points.

paragraphs: Games involving neural-network strategies or utilities can be non-concave, making familiar equilibrium concepts difficult to compute. Some equilibria may fail to exist, while others exist but are intractable. This paper investigates whether a more flexible solution concept can provide efficiently approachable outcomes in such games.

A Φ-equilibrium is defined relative to a chosen family of strategy modifications. This family determines the deviations against which the outcome is assessed. Although existence is already established even for non-concave games, computational tractability remains a separate question. The paper studies several natural modification families to identify settings where learning can efficiently approximate these equilibria.

For a finite family Φ, the authors show that an efficient uncoupled learning algorithm can approximate the corresponding equilibrium. They also consider infinite families made up of local modifications and establish that Online Gradient Descent works efficiently in non-trivial regimes. The results provide tractable alternatives under specified deviation families, rather than claiming efficient computation of every standard equilibrium in arbitrary non-concave games.
neurips-2024-on-tractable-phi-equilibria.tldr: The paper identifies strategy-modification families for which Φ-equilibria in non-concave games can be approximated efficiently.

paragraphs: Referring tasks connect a phrase to the image region it describes, either by locating the target or segmenting it. OneRef addresses the complexity of systems that encode images and language separately and then require elaborate mechanisms to combine them. It uses one shared Transformer tower to place visual and linguistic features in a unified space.

Its training scheme, Mask Referring Modeling, includes both image masking and language masking that are aware of the referring relationship. Reconstruction covers content within each modality as well as referring content across modalities. The image masking strategy also adapts to the referred region, instead of depending on a fixed masking ratio or generic random selection.

These choices are intended to teach the model which visual content a phrase refers to, beyond simply recovering missing image or text information. The shared representation then supports direct prediction of referring outputs. The authors report consistently surpassing existing approaches and achieving state-of-the-art performance on both grounding and segmentation, supporting the effectiveness of this unified design.
neurips-2024-oneref-unified-one-tower-ex.tldr: OneRef combines a shared image-language Transformer with referring-aware masked training to improve expression grounding and segmentation.

paragraphs: Generative language models can influence the labor market through the application materials job seekers produce, as well as through tools employers use. This paper examines social bias in ChatGPT-generated job applications. Its experimental design simulates application writing in response to real job advertisements, allowing the researchers to study language elicited by diverse postings.

The authors introduce a quantitative evaluation framework based on masked language models and validated inventories of social cues and words. This provides a systematic way to assess bias in the generated text. The focus is on language patterns appearing in application materials, connecting the evaluation directly to a plausible use of generative AI by job seekers.

The findings indicate that biased and gendered language in these materials can reinforce or exacerbate gender and social inequalities. This identifies a potential pathway by which wider AI adoption could reproduce labor-market disparities. The contribution combines a realistic prompting setup with a structured measurement approach, showing why applicant-side use deserves attention alongside employer-side automation.
neurips-2024-probing-social-bias-in-labo.tldr: The study uses masked language models to assess social bias in ChatGPT-written job applications and identifies language that can reinforce labor-market inequalities.

paragraphs: Optimization on Lie groups must respect the structure of the space in which the variables live. This paper studies momentum-based optimization dynamics and algorithms obtained by discretizing those dynamics while preserving that structure. It analyzes an existing scheme, Lie Heavy-Ball, and introduces a new one, Lie NAG-SC.

The authors explicitly quantify convergence rates under smoothness and local strong convexity assumptions. Within this analysis, Lie NAG-SC accelerates convergence relative to Riemannian gradient descent, the momentumless comparison. Lie Heavy-Ball does not provide that acceleration. The distinction shows that adding momentum alone does not establish the same rate improvement for both discretizations.

Both algorithms use the group structure to simplify computation compared with existing accelerated methods for general manifolds. They require a gradient oracle and an exponential map, avoiding logarithm maps and parallel transport, which the abstract identifies as costly. The contribution therefore combines conditional convergence guarantees with simpler computational requirements, while tying the acceleration result specifically to Lie NAG-SC under the stated assumptions.
neurips-2024-quantitative-convergences-o.tldr: Under smoothness and local strong convexity, Lie NAG-SC achieves accelerated convergence using Lie-group structure and relatively simple operations.

paragraphs: Adversarial perturbations can disrupt deployed neural networks, while conventional robustness training can demand substantial computation. This paper formulates the Rapid Plug-in Defender problem: adapting a defense quickly without modifying the deployed target model. The aim is to make responses to attacks more agile.

The proposed method, CeTaD, uses a pretrained Transformer as the defender. It fine-tunes the defender’s normalization-layer parameters using a limited collection of clean and adversarial examples. Restricting adaptation to these parameters is central to the method’s emphasis on computational efficiency, while leaving the target model unchanged.

The evaluation examines effectiveness, transferability, and component contributions in settings involving one-shot adversarial examples. It also studies how training-data conditions affect performance. The authors report rapid adaptation across attacks and application scenarios, with adaptability across differentiable service models. They further identify potential for continuous learning. These findings support the use of an adaptable external defender when changing or extensively retraining the deployed model would hinder a quick response.
neurips-2024-rapid-plug-in-defenders-7b3.tldr: CeTaD rapidly adapts a pretrained Transformer defender by tuning normalization parameters while leaving the deployed target model unchanged.

paragraphs: Sequential decision-making can be approached by generating trajectories conditioned on what a user wants. Existing return-conditioned diffusion approaches depend on well-defined reward functions, which require human effort and can be difficult to specify across multiple tasks. This paper instead considers preferences as the information used to guide behavior.

The proposed framework learns representations aligned with preference labels across tasks. Those representations become conditions for a diffusion model’s generation process. This connects preference learning with trajectory generation: the model receives a learned encoding of the desired preference, rather than relying only on a target return supplied by a reward function.

The authors identify a consistency problem in conventional classifier-free guidance: generated trajectories may not agree with their conditions. They introduce an auxiliary regularization objective aimed at strengthening that connection. The supplied abstract ends while describing its mutual-information objective, so it provides no completed formulation or experimental findings. The supported contribution is the proposed combination of multi-task preference representations, conditional diffusion, and regularization addressing condition–trajectory consistency.
neurips-2024-regularized-conditional-dif.tldr: The paper proposes preference-conditioned diffusion with auxiliary regularization to better align generated trajectories with preferences across tasks.

paragraphs: Constrained reinforcement learning often represents unsafe behavior with a separate cost function, but specifying and evaluating that function can be expensive. This paper learns it from feedback collected between training rounds. Feedback can come from a system or a human and can describe a whole trajectory, reducing the need to assess individual states.

Whole-trajectory feedback creates a credit-assignment problem: a judgment about a sequence does not directly identify which states caused concern. The authors introduce a surrogate objective that turns this into supervised state classification with noisy labels. They also use novelty-based sampling to select trajectories for evaluation and stop querying when trajectories are no longer novel.

Experiments cover Safety Gymnasium benchmarks and realistic self-driving scenarios. Using only trajectory-level feedback, the method achieves reported near-optimal performance comparable to learning with a known cost function. The results support learning useful safety costs with a reduced evaluator burden, while the novelty mechanism addresses both which trajectories to present and when additional requests are no longer needed.
neurips-2024-safety-through-feedback-in-.tldr: The method learns safety costs from trajectory-level feedback and uses novelty-based queries to reduce evaluation effort.

paragraphs: Communication about an observation can require referring to one part in relation to another. This paper studies whether artificial agents can develop messages that express such spatial relationships. The agents train in a referential game designed to require this kind of communication, making relational information necessary for the task.

The trained agents achieve more than 90% accuracy. To investigate how their messages work, the authors use a collocation measure to examine patterns in the emergent language. The analysis suggests a mixture of compositional and non-compositional messages: some spatial meanings arise through combinations of message elements, while others are conveyed through less decomposable expressions.

The paper also tests whether humans can interpret the language well enough to communicate with a receiver agent. Using parts of the interpreted lexicon, the receiver achieves more than 78% accuracy. This provides a behavioral check on the proposed interpretation, beyond inspecting messages alone. The results demonstrate spatial reference and partial human interpretability within the studied communication setting.
neurips-2024-speaking-your-language-spat.tldr: Agents learn to communicate spatial relationships in a referential game, and a partially interpreted lexicon enables successful human-to-agent communication.

paragraphs: Temporal graphs represent relationships that change over time, often with several kinds of entities or connections. TGB 2.0 provides a framework for evaluating predictions of future links in temporal knowledge graphs and temporal heterogeneous graphs. It addresses both the shortage of large benchmark datasets and difficulties reproducing evaluation protocols.

The benchmark introduces eight datasets across five domains, with the largest scale reaching 53 million edges. The datasets expand on existing resources in numbers of nodes, edges, or timestamps. A shared evaluation pipeline is intended to make comparisons more reproducible and realistic for graphs containing multiple relationship types.

The experiments produce three notable findings. Using edge-type information is crucial for strong performance, simple heuristics are often competitive with more complex models, and most evaluated methods cannot run on the largest datasets. Together, these observations make the benchmark useful for assessing both predictive quality and practical scalability. They also show why model complexity alone is insufficient evidence of a better solution for these temporal prediction tasks.
neurips-2024-tgb-2-0-a-benchmark-for-lea.tldr: TGB 2.0 benchmarks large temporal graphs and finds that relationship types, competitive heuristics, and scalability deserve greater attention.

paragraphs: Understanding whether a meeting conversation remains relevant to its topics could help investigate meeting effectiveness. This paper introduces the Topic-Conversation Relevance dataset to support that task. Its focus is the relationship between meeting transcripts and topics, giving researchers material for evaluating whether models recognize on-topic discussion.

TCR brings together 1,500 unique meetings, 22 million transcript words, and more than 15,000 meeting topics. It combines newly collected Speech Interruption Meeting data with existing public datasets and covers different domains and meeting styles. This diversity provides a broader basis for evaluation than a collection drawn from a single kind of meeting.

The authors also release scripts for generating synthetic meetings and augmenting existing TCR meetings to increase data diversity. For each source, they create benchmarks using GPT-4 to evaluate transcription-topic relevance accuracy. The contribution is a dataset, supporting generation tools, and reference evaluations for studying topic relevance; the abstract motivates this through meeting effectiveness without reporting that the resource itself improves meeting outcomes.
neurips-2024-topic-conversation-relevanc.tldr: TCR supplies diverse meeting transcripts, topics, augmentation tools, and GPT-4 benchmarks for evaluating conversation relevance.

paragraphs: Linear probing followed by fine-tuning first trains a classifier head and then adapts the model more broadly. This paper analyzes why that sequence works well for language-model classification, using neural tangent kernel theory. The analysis focuses on preserving pretrained features while adapting the model to a task.

By decomposing the neural tangent kernel matrix into two components, the authors show that the linear head’s norm matters alongside its initial prediction accuracy. They observe that cross-entropy training during linear probing substantially increases this norm. The larger norm reduces changes to learned features during subsequent fine-tuning, providing an explanation beyond simply obtaining a good initial classifier.

The increased norm also has a downside: it can harm calibration, meaning the model’s confidence becomes less reliable. The authors report that temperature scaling can correct this effect. They extend the analysis to low-rank adaptation and validate it with Transformer experiments across multiple language datasets. The findings connect the benefits of the two-stage procedure with a specific training mechanism and its confidence-related consequence.
neurips-2024-understanding-linear-probin.tldr: An NTK analysis links LP-FT’s feature preservation to growth in the classifier-head norm, while identifying a calibration cost correctable by temperature scaling.

paragraphs: Offboard perception aims to generate high-quality 3D labels for autonomous-driving scenes. Existing approaches concentrate on object detection within fixed category sets, while changing perception tasks require broader recognition. ZOPP proposes a unified framework for automatically labeling varied scene elements, motivated by reliance on human labels and problems of sparse or imbalanced data.

The framework combines the zero-shot recognition capabilities of vision foundation models with 3D representations derived from point clouds. This brings visual recognition and spatial information into a multimodal panoptic perception approach. Its intended role is to support auto-labeling across the different needs of autonomous-driving perception tasks.

The authors evaluate ZOPP on the Waymo open dataset across multiple perception tasks. They also conduct downstream experiments to investigate usability and extensibility beyond the initial evaluations. The reported results indicate potential for real-world use. The contribution is the integration of foundation-model recognition with point-cloud-based 3D information in an offboard labeling framework, supported by empirical studies of its proposed uses.
neurips-2024-zopp-a-framework-of-zero-sh.tldr: ZOPP combines zero-shot visual recognition with point-cloud representations for offboard panoptic perception and automatic labeling of driving scenes.
